title: Pagination and infinite scroll
summary: Use cursor-based pagination for feeds that change while you scroll; offset pagination skips or duplicates items when new ones are inserted. Prefetch ahead and dedupe by ID on the client.
requirements: Smooth infinite scroll with no duplicates or gaps while new items arrive.
Pull to refresh for newer items; resume from cache on relaunch.
components: Client paginator: state machine (idle, loading, error, exhausted) per direction
Prefetch trigger when the user is N items from the end
Local cache of pages keyed by feed + cursor
tradeoffs: Offset/limit is simple and supports jumping to page N, but is unstable for live data and slow for deep pages on the server.
Cursor (opaque, encodes sort key + id) is stable and efficient; cannot jump to arbitrary pages.
Bigger pages mean fewer requests but slower first paint and more wasted data.
body: **Gaps:** when refreshing the top after being away, the server may return a page that does not connect to cached items. Detect (last new item not in cache) and show a 'load more' gap marker or drop the stale cache.
**Dedup:** merge by stable ID; diffable data sources make updates animate correctly.
**Errors:** keep loaded items, show inline retry at the bottom; never block the whole list.
**Performance:** cap items in memory for very long sessions (window the list), prefetch images for upcoming cells.
